cells.question: Q01
cells.note: The card prints no issue or revision date. The inherited population dates its earliest located publication to 2025-02 by index month; that is not a printed card date.

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: When using Claude on Claude.AI or via the API, Claude’s reasoning in extended thinking appears in a separate section before its final response.

cells.note: The card describes consumer and API use, without a calendar release date.

search.read: Introduction, §1.2 and §§1.4.2–1.4.4; whole-card date and availability search

cells.question: Q03

passages.quote: Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy. https://www.anthropic.com/index/anthropics-responsible-scaling-policy, September 2023.

cells.note: The bibliography identifies the cited RSP by September 2023. This records the card’s reference, without substituting a later edition.

cells.question: Q04

passages.quote: https://www.anthropic.com/index/anthropics-responsible-scaling-policy

cells.note: The card supplies the policy address.

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: Based on our assessments, we’ve concluded that Claude 3.7 Sonnet is released under the ASL-2 standard.

cells.note: The card reports an ASL-2 safeguards determination.

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: Claude 3.7 Sonnet is sufficiently far away from the ASL-3 capability thresholds such that ASL-2 safeguards remain appropriate.
passages.locator: §1.4.4 ASL-2 Determination and Conclusions, PDF p. 7

cells.note: The card ties ASL-2 safeguards to its assessment against ASL-3 capability thresholds.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: Altogether, we believe that Claude 3.7 Sonnet continues to be sufficiently far away from the ASL-3 capability thresholds, and therefore, we find that ASL-2 safeguards remain appropriate.

cells.note: The card’s biological-risk conclusion is recorded at policy level. §7.1.1 states that chemical risks were not evaluated directly; §7.1.2 describes nuclear-risk work with NNSA.

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: Because the model did not have wide success in medium difficulty evaluations, we did not conduct evaluations on the hardest tasks.
passages.locator: §7.3 Cyber Evaluations, Results item 3, PDF p. 35

cells.note: The card reports a qualitative outcome of its offensive-cyber evaluations; no task contents or scores are recorded.

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: these improvements did not cross any new capability thresholds beyond those already reached by Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new).

cells.note: The card reports its autonomy/AI R&D evaluation conclusion.

cells.question: Q10
cells.note: No passage meeting the criterion was found in the recorded search.

search.read: §§5.1–5.3 on faithfulness, concerning thought processes and alignment faking; §§7.1–7.4 on RSP evaluations; whole-card search

setAside.reason: Monitoring includes deception, omission and sycophancy in the model’s reasoning; it does not report an evaluation of persuasive or manipulative capability toward people.

cells.question: Q11

passages.quote: During our evaluations we noticed that Claude 3.7 Sonnet occasionally resorts to special-casing in order to pass test cases in agentic coding environments like Claude Code.
passages.locator: §6 Excessive Focus on Passing Tests, PDF p. 22

cells.note: The card reports reward-hacking behaviour observed during evaluations.

cells.question: Q12

passages.quote: Our evaluations were informed by our previous deployment and included both internal and third-party red-teaming exercises as well as automated evaluations.

cells.note: The stated scope is computer-use risk; internal and third-party red-teaming are reported.

cells.question: Q13

passages.quote: Domain experts from Deloitte engaged in extended conversations with Claude

cells.note: The card names Deloitte as an external evaluator; technical evaluation details are omitted.

cells.question: Q14

passages.quote: the U.S. AI Safety Institute (U.S. AISI) and U.K. AI Security Institute (U.K. AISI) conducted pre-deployment testing of Claude 3.7 Sonnet

cells.note: The named institutes are reported to have tested the model.

cells.question: Q15

passages.quote: Consistent with our RSP, the RSO and CEO made the ultimate determination on the model’s ASL.

cells.note: The named makers are attached to the ASL determination, rather than an expressly attributed release decision. This is the criterion’s capability/safeguards-determination case under decision 6a; availability alone does not count (13a).

setAside.reason: The final-release verification requirement describes a process, rather than who made this release decision.

cells.question: Q16

passages.quote: how the model performs on expert-level evaluations may not directly translate to real-world capabilities

cells.note: The card limits interpretation of its evaluation results.

cells.question: Q01

passages.quote: May 2025

cells.note: The card’s cover carries a month, without a day or a printed revision date.

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: This style of prompting is not possible in Claude.ai and similar chat interfaces, but it is accessible to developers through our API.
passages.locator: §4.1.7 Jailbreak and prefill susceptibility, PDF p. 42

cells.note: The card implies API access in a passage on a jailbreak prompting technique; it states no release form or release date. The cover’s “May 2025” is the card’s date (Q01), not a release date.

crossFamily.result: minor, applied: the passage concerns a prompting technique and implies API access only; the earlier note (“identifies consumer and API access forms”) overstated it.

cells.question: Q03

passages.quote: please see the Responsible Scaling Policy
passages.locator: §1.2.3 AI Safety Level determination process, PDF p. 9 (hyperlink annotation on policy name)

cells.note: The card’s hyperlink annotation targets https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/872c653b2d0501d6ab44cf87f43e1dc4853e4d37.pdf. The target’s cover prints Version 2.2, Effective May 14, 2025. Edition identified by link annotation under decision 4a; recorded as rsp-v2-2.

cells.question: Q04

passages.quote: For more information on the requirements for these ASL Standards, please see the Responsible Scaling Policy

cells.note: The framework name in this passage is linked directly to the RSP v2.2 PDF. Page 8 separately links a policy-update announcement; that is not the edition evidence.

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: we have decided to release Claude Opus 4 under the ASL-3 Standard and Claude Sonnet 4 under the ASL-2 Standard.
passages.locator: §1.2.3 AI Safety Level determination process, PDF p. 9

cells.note: The card applies different safeguard standards to the two models. For Opus 4 the card says ASL-3 capability could not be ruled out, rather than reporting that it definitively passed the threshold (§1.2.4).

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: The ASL-3 safeguards we have now activated for Claude Opus 4 represent significant investments in both deployment protections and security controls

cells.note: The card ties the stated deployment and security controls to Opus 4’s precautionary ASL-3 deployment.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: we cannot clearly rule out ASL-3 risks for Claude Opus 4 (although we have ruled out that it needs the ASL-4 Standard).

cells.note: The conclusion concerns CBRN capability uncertainty described in §§1.2.3–1.2.4. Sonnet 4 remains at ASL-2; this is not a claim that Opus 4 definitively passed the ASL-3 capability threshold.

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: Based on the evaluation results, we believe the models do not demonstrate catastrophically risky capabilities in the cyber domain.

cells.note: The card’s policy-level conclusion covers both models. §7.4 states that the RSP has no formal cyber threshold at any ASL level.

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: Claude Opus 4 shows improvement over Claude Sonnet 3.7 in most AI research and software engineering capabilities, while remaining below the ASL-4 Autonomy threshold.

cells.note: The card concludes that Opus 4 remains below the ASL-4 autonomy threshold; the Sonnet 4 conclusion on p. 106 also says ASL-4 protections are not required.

cells.question: Q10

passages.quote: In this assessment, we aim to detect a cluster of related phenomena including: … attempts to manipulate users toward certain views. We conducted testing continuously throughout finetuning

cells.note: The card includes user manipulation in the alignment assessment’s scope. A separate outcome for that capability was not found; this is not a reported human persuasion trial.

setAside.reason: The emotional-manipulation metric concerns an AI auditor, not a person.

cells.question: Q11

passages.quote: None of the snapshots we tested showed significant signs of systematic deception or coherent hidden goals.

cells.note: This is the card’s aggregate conclusion for Opus 4 snapshots. The same section and §4.1.1 describe conditional self-preservation and deception findings; it is not a conclusion that such behaviour was absent.

cells.question: Q12

passages.quote: Red-teamers probed various scenarios over three days of testing
passages.locator: §7.2.4.2 ASL-3 expert red teaming, PDF p. 94

cells.note: The card reports biological-risk expert red-teaming by Deloitte for both models, over three days.

cells.question: Q13

passages.quote: we contracted with Apollo Research to assess an early snapshot for propensities and capabilities related to sabotage

cells.note: The named external evaluation concerns an early Opus 4 snapshot; its findings are not attributed to the final model.

cells.question: Q14

passages.quote: joint pre-deployment testing of the new Claude Opus 4 model was conducted by the US AI Safety Institute (US AISI) and the UK AI Security Institute (UK AISI).

cells.note: This passage concerns Opus 4; it does not state that the institutes also tested Sonnet 4.

cells.question: Q15

passages.quote: Based on these assessments, we have decided to release Claude Opus 4 under the ASL-3 Standard and Claude Sonnet 4 under the ASL-2 Standard.

cells.note: The card expressly states a release decision. The developer’s “we” identifies Anthropic as decision-maker under decision 6a; CEO/RSO roles in the preceding paragraph concern the ASL determination.

cells.question: Q16

passages.quote: The absolute values of these metrics depend on our largely-arbitrary choice of auditor instructions.

cells.note: The card limits interpretation of its automated behavioural audit metrics.
